subtitle: Snow, Steel and a Silent Throne

panels.shot: split composition, left half a stormy mountain battlefield, right half a dim Ladakhi throne room
panels.action: On one side, Zorawar Singh stands in layered mountain armour on a snowy ridge, wind tearing at his banner; on the other, Tshepal Namgyal sits small on a high Ladakhi throne, shadowed monks and mountains behind.

dialogue.text: In the high desert of Ladakh, Zorawar Singh’s march ended a dynasty, and left Tshepal Namgyal a king without a kingdom.

i18n.hi: लद्दाख के ऊँचे रेगिस्तान में ज़ोरावर की चढ़ाई ने एक वंश मिटाया, और छेपल नमग्याल को बे–रियासत राजा बना छोड़ा।

panels.shot: wide aerial of the Indus cutting through Ladakh’s barren mountains at dusk
panels.action: The Indus River glints like a silver ribbon between stark brown ridges, scattered white monasteries clinging to cliffs, tiny fields of green pressed against the water under a vast darkening sky.

dialogue.text: For centuries, the Namgyal kings held Ladakh’s high valleys, trading between Kashmir, Tibet and Central Asia, as caravans followed the Indus through wind-scoured rock.

i18n.hi: सदियों तक नमग्याल राजा लद्दाख की ऊँची घाटियों के मालिक थे, जब काफ़िले कश्मीर, तिब्बत और मध्य एशिया के बीच सिंधु के साथ–साथ चलते थे।

panels.shot: medium inside Leh palace audience hall, emphasis on Tshepal Namgyal
panels.action: Tshepal Namgyal, robed in rich but worn brocade, sits on a raised throne in Leh’s wooden-pillared hall, courtiers and monks around him, his face thoughtful as light filters in from high windows.

dialogue.text: By the early 1800s, their power had thinned. Trade shifted, tribute weighed heavy, and Tshepal Namgyal inherited a throne hemmed in by stronger neighbours.

i18n.hi: १८०० के शुरू तक उनकी ताक़त घिस चुकी थी। व्यापार खिसक गया, नज़राने भारी हो गए, और छेपल नमग्याल को ऐसा तख़्त मिला जो चारों ओर ताक़तवर पड़ोसियों से घिरा था।

panels.shot: map-like overhead morphing into a court scene in Jammu
panels.action: A stylised map shows Jammu, Lahore and Leh linked by routes; this dissolves into Gulab Singh’s court in Jammu where armoured Dogra officers stand over a spread of maps and mountain sketches.

dialogue.text: In the south, Gulab Singh of Jammu, rising under Maharaja Ranjit Singh’s Sikh empire, saw these passes as the key to trade, revenue and prestige.

i18n.hi: दक्षिण में जम्मू के गुलाब सिंह, महाराजा रणजीत सिंह की सिख सल्तनत में ऊभरते हुए, इन दर्रों को व्यापार, आमदनी और शान की चाबी मानते थे।

panels.shot: close on Zorawar Singh in Gulab Singh’s court, low-angle
panels.action: Zorawar Singh, compact and hard-eyed in quilted armour and wool, stands before an unseen ruler, one hand resting on a rolled map, his expression steady and confident.

dialogue.text: To seize it, Gulab Singh chose his fiercest lieutenant, Zorawar Singh, whose campaigns in the hills of Kishtwar had already made his name a mountain legend.

i18n.hi: इसे हथियाने के लिए गुलाब सिंह ने अपना सबसे दिलेर सिपहसालार चुना – ज़ोरावर सिंह, जिसकी किश्तवाड़ की पहाड़ियों वाली लड़ाइयों ने उसे पहाड़ों की दास्तान बना दिया था।

panels.shot: long shot of Dogra troops climbing a high pass, Zorawar in foreground
panels.action: Columns of Dogra soldiers in layered wool and leather file up a narrow snow-dusted path, pack animals laden behind them; Zorawar Singh leads on horseback, wrapped in furs, eyes scanning the frozen heights.

dialogue.text: In 1834, Zorawar marched through Kishtwar and over the high passes into Ladakh, his army hauling guns and grain where air was thin and every step could kill.

i18n.hi: १८३४ में ज़ोरावर किश्तवाड़ से निकलकर ऊँचे दर्रों को पार करता लद्दाख में घुसा, उसकी फौज पतली हवा में तोपें और राशन घसीटती, जहाँ हर क़दम जान ले सकता था।

panels.shot: broad view of Leh town with Dogra forces at its edge
panels.action: Leh town sprawls beneath its palace, whitewashed houses and stupas under a pale sky; Dogra troops line up outside, their standards planted, Ladakhi envoys approaching between the two sides.

dialogue.text: The Namgyal forces could not match this push. After hard fighting in the valleys, the Dogras reached Leh, and Tshepal Namgyal’s position collapsed.

i18n.hi: नमग्याल की फौजें ये धक्का झेल न सकीं। घाटियों में सख़्त लड़ाइयों के बाद डोगरे लेह पहुँच गए, और छेपल नमग्याल की हालत टूट गई।

panels.shot: intimate medium shot inside Leh palace as Tshepal meets Zorawar
panels.action: In the audience hall, Tshepal Namgyal stands, shoulders tense, facing Zorawar Singh, who has removed his helmet; between them on a low table lies a folded treaty and ritual objects.

dialogue.text: “Keep my throne’s name, if not its power,” Tshepal Namgyal murmurs.

i18n.hi: “मेरे तख़्त का नाम बचा रहे, चाहें ताक़त न रहे,” छेपल नमग्याल बुदबुदाता है।

panels.shot: mid-wide of Leh palace courtyard with Dogra and Ladakhi retinues
panels.action: In the palace courtyard, Dogra officers stand beside Ladakhi nobles and monks; Zorawar Singh watches as Tshepal Namgyal performs a formal gesture of submission, attendants holding gifts and documents nearby.

dialogue.text: Tshepal was left as a figurehead under Dogra control, then pensioned off. Real authority passed to Zorawar’s officers, as the Namgyal kingdom was folded into Jammu’s growing domain.

i18n.hi: छेपल को डोगरा हुक्म में सिर्फ़ मुखिया भर छोड़ दिया गया, फिर पेंशन पर हटा दिया गया। असली हक़ूमत ज़ोरावर के अफ़सरों के पास चली गई, और नमग्याल रियासत जम्मू की बढ़ती हद में समा गई।

panels.shot: contrasting split scene: monastery courtyard and Dogra camp office
panels.action: On one side, monks stand in a monastery courtyard as Dogra officials catalogue stacked grain and metal objects; on the other, in a tent, a Dogra clerk writes accounts while Zorawar reviews lists beside drawn-up tax tables.

dialogue.text: Monastery records later spoke of looted stores, forced labour and seized estates. Dogra records praised new revenue systems and the channeling of Ladakh’s wealth towards Jammu.

i18n.hi: मठों के दर्ज़ों में बाद में लूटे गए भंडार, जबरन मज़दूरी और छीनी गई ज़मीनों की बात आई। डोगरा काग़ज़ों में नई महसूली व्यवस्था की वाहवाही थी, और ये कि लद्दाख की दौलत अब जम्मू की तरफ़ बह रही थी।

panels.shot: medium on Ladakhi villagers working on a road under guard
panels.action: Ladakhi villagers haul stones and timber along a rough track under the watch of a few Dogra soldiers, snow peaks looming; Tshepal Namgyal passes in a palanquin, looking out with a distant, troubled gaze.

dialogue.text: Oral traditions remembered corvée labour and burdens heavier than before. In the same years, Dogra storytellers sang of Zorawar’s iron will that bent cold, rock and people to command.

i18n.hi: लोक कहानियों में बेगार और पहले से भारी बोझ याद रहे। उन्हीं बरसों में डोगरा कहानीकार ज़ोरावर की लोहे सी जिद गाते रहे, जिसने सर्दी, पत्थर और लोगों को झुका लिया।

panels.shot: close-up on Zorawar looking at a map that extends beyond Ladakh into Tibet
panels.action: Zorawar sits by a brazier in a high camp, a rough map of Ladakh and western Tibet spread before him, his finger tracing the routes eastward, eyes alight with ambition.

dialogue.text: Control of Ladakh whetted larger aims. Beyond lay western Tibet, under Lhasa and the distant Qing, and with it more trade routes, salt lakes and prestige.

i18n.hi: लद्दाख पर पकड़ ने और बड़े मन्सूबे जगा दिए। आगे पश्चिमी तिब्बत था, ल्हासा और दूर बैठे चिंग के अधीन, साथ ही नए व्यापार रास्ते, नमक झीलें और इज़्ज़त।

panels.shot: wide of Dogra columns entering the Tibetan plateau, stark landscape
panels.action: Dogra columns advance across a bleak, frozen plain, fluttering prayer flags on distant ridges, icy wind whipping cloaks; Zorawar rides at their head, jaw set, as yak caravans watch from afar.

dialogue.text: In 1841, he led his men into western Tibet, taking forts and settlements in a bold winter campaign that alarmed Lhasa and drew in Tibetan and Qing-backed forces.

i18n.hi: १८४१ में वह फौज लेकर पश्चिमी तिब्बत में घुसा, क़िलों और बस्तियों पर कब्ज़ा करता, एक दिलेर सर्दी के सफ़र में जिसने ल्हासा को चौंका दिया और तिब्बती व चिंग–समर्थ फौजों को मैदान में खींच लाया।

panels.shot: chaotic wide shot of the battle near Toyo, snowstorm obscuring detail
panels.action: In a blinding snowstorm near Toyo, Dogra and Tibetan forces clash in the whiteout, silhouettes struggling through drifts; Zorawar Singh is glimpsed in mid-charge, partially obscured by swirling snow.

dialogue.text: Then, in the snows near Toyo, the balance broke. In harsh cold and thin air, Tibetan resistance and winter itself shattered Zorawar’s army, and he fell in battle.

i18n.hi: फिर टोयो के पास की बर्फ़ में बाज़ी पलट गई। कड़ी सर्दी और पतली हवा में, तिब्बती मज़ाहमत और खुद सर्दी ने ज़ोरावर की फौज तोड़ दी, और वह जंग में गिर पड़ा।

panels.shot: somber medium of Dogra survivors retreating through a pass
panels.action: A reduced, weary band of Dogra soldiers trudges back through a narrow pass, faces gaunt, some supporting the weak, distant monasteries watching from the cliffs above.

dialogue.text: Survivors staggered back into Ladakh. Their defeat checked further advance, and forced negotiations between Jammu, Lhasa and the representatives of the weakening Qing order.

i18n.hi: बचे–खुचे सिपाही लड़खड़ाते लद्दाख लौटे। उनकी शिकस्त ने आगे की बढ़त रोक दी, और जम्मू, ल्हासा और ढहती चिंग सल्तनत के नुमाइंदों के बीच सुलह पर मजबूर कर दिया।

panels.shot: composed scene of Tibetan, Dogra and British-influenced envoys over a map
panels.action: Envoys from Jammu and Tibet sit across a low table with a map marking Ladakh and the frontier; a British-style officer stands to one side, observing, while hands point to the old boundary lines.

dialogue.text: By 1842, a settlement restored the old frontier between Ladakh and Tibet. Ladakh remained with Jammu, but the snowline now marked a mutually watched, carefully noted border.

i18n.hi: १८४२ तक एक समझौते ने लद्दाख और तिब्बत की पुरानी सरहद लौटा दी। लद्दाख जम्मू के पास रहा, पर अब हिम–रेखा ही दोनों तरफ़ से तकी हुई, दर्ज की गई हद बन गई।

panels.shot: medium inside Leh palace years later, Tshepal older and quieter
panels.action: An older Tshepal Namgyal sits in a quieter corner of the palace, now less crowded, looking over the town of Leh from a window as Dogra officials pass below in the courtyard.

dialogue.text: Tshepal lived on under Dogra protection, drawing a pension, his line’s authority ended. In Leh, people now bowed to Jammu’s officers, even as they still whispered of the Namgyals.

i18n.hi: छेपल डोगरा हिफ़ाज़त में पेंशन लेते जीता रहा, उसके ख़ानदान की हकूमत ख़त्म हो चुकी थी। लेह में लोग अब जम्मू के अफ़सरों को झुकते, पर धीमे स्वर में अभी भी नमग्यालों का ज़िक्र करते।

panels.shot: documentary-style close-up of the Treaty of Amritsar being signed
panels.action: A hand holding a quill signs a Persian-script document, other hands pressing seals; in the background, British officials in frock coats and Dogra nobles in turbans regard each other carefully.

dialogue.text: In 1846, the Treaty of Amritsar between the British and Gulab Singh recognised him as Maharaja of Jammu and Kashmir, with Ladakh inside this new princely state.

i18n.hi: १८४६ में अंग्रेज़ों और गुलाब सिंह के बीच अमृतसर की संधि ने उसे महाराजा जम्मू–कश्मीर माना, जिसमें लद्दाख भी इस नए रियासती सूबे के अंदर था।

panels.shot: present-day style wide of Leh with palace, monastery and modern traces, ghostly overlays of Zorawar and Tshepal
panels.action: Modern Leh spreads around the old palace and monasteries, with roads and scattered new buildings; faint, translucent figures of Zorawar Singh in armour and Tshepal Namgyal in robes look in opposite directions over the town.

dialogue.text: Today, Ladakh’s place in India and the Himalaya still rests on frontiers drawn in those years, and Zorawar Singh and Tshepal Namgyal are remembered differently along the same cold wind.

i18n.hi: आज भी भारत और हिमालय में लद्दाख की जगह उन ही बरसों में बनी सरहदों पर टिकी है, और ज़ोरावर सिंह व छेपल नमग्याल को उसी ठंडी हवा के दो किनारों पर अलग–अलग तरह से याद किया जाता है।

title_i18n.en: Zorawar Singh Ends the Namgyal Kingdom
title_i18n.hi: ज़ोरावर सिंह ने खत्म किया नमग्याल राज

subtitle_i18n.en: Snow, Steel and a Silent Throne
